summary: Nothing new that changes Alphabet's cash flows since the post-print update: its quarterly SEC report (10-Q, filed Oct 29) matches the earnings release already used, and the extras (a USD 5.0B loan taken by Waymo that Alphabet does not guarantee, up to USD 6.6B of chip buy-back promises to TPU customers) are small. Analysts cut targets (Citi 447 to 375, Wells Fargo 417 to 371, Bernstein 385 to 325, Morgan Stanley 400 to 375), still mostly above our research target (12m) of 329.15; the stock fell 12.6% on Oct 29 and another 1.4% to 279.76 on Oct 30 with the tech selloff, with no new company facts.

items.headline: Alphabet Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Sep 30, 2026 filed
items.why: I opened it. It matches the Oct 28 release: revenue 127,577M, Cloud 30,709M, capex 51.4B, operating cash flow 42.3B, ATM 12.4B of proceeds for 36M shares, no share buy-backs, SpaceX shares 75.2B in marketable equity (total 90.4B), non-marketable equity at cost-basis method 128.2B, long-term debt 125.1B, purchase commitments 924.4B (213.4B due within 12 months) and 130.5B of leases not yet started. The research already ran a 10-Q pass on Oct 29 (stake marks, clicks, backlog), so nothing here is new to the numbers. DOJ search appeals and ad-tech cases are unchanged; the EU Android fine (5.2B) was paid in July.

items.headline: 10-Q subsequent event: Waymo signs a USD 5.0B senior secured term loan (Oct 2026, matures Oct 2032, Term SOFR + 5.25%), not guaranteed by Alphabet
items.why: Not found in the research files. It adds about 5B of cash and debt together (about 0.4 a share of debt if all counted), secured on Waymo assets with no recourse to Alphabet. It shows Waymo is funding growth with outside debt rather than from the parent, which slightly lowers the parent cash call. Not sized in the research target (12m); the effect at any date is small against 329.

items.headline: 10-Q: Alphabet guarantees to buy back TPU systems if customers return them, maximum 6.6B
items.why: New disclosure not in the research files. Alphabet says the fair value of the promise is not material and the buy-back price is at a discount, so it expects no exercise. If it were used, up to 6.6B (about 0.5 a share) would flow out at some later date; I could not size the chance.

items.headline: Analyst target changes after the print: Citigroup 447 to 375 (buy), Wells Fargo 417 to 371 (overweight), Bernstein 385 to 325 (market perform), Morgan Stanley 400 to 375 (overweight); Goldman Sachs buy 385
items.why: One aggregator only (a second MarketBeat page agrees on Wells Fargo); the notes themselves were not read. These are opinions inside the agents' range. All sit above or near our research target (12m) of 329.15 except Bernstein at 325. No new facts. The Morgan Stanley digest folder has no Alphabet note in the window.

items.headline: Alphabet shares fell 12.6% on Oct 29 (324.89 to 283.82) and 1.4% on Oct 30 to 279.76; Intel -29% and AI-spending worries drove the tech selloff
items.why: Price move only. Prices from the market data quote for Oct 29 and Oct 30; Forbes confirms the Oct 29 drop and the Intel-led selloff. Forbes and the Yahoo Finance October wipeout piece give no new Alphabet facts. Thesis break is 250; the close is 279.76.

items.headline: Post-print commentary: Gemini app at 1 billion users, nearly 100 TPU customers including Apple and Anthropic, Search ad revenue +12% to 63.35B
items.why: Restates call and release facts the update round already used (Search +12%, TPU partners). The customer count and user count are single-outlet and unverified. Not used.
